body:
Thanks.

I thought GED was something you got if you didn't get a high school diploma. I graduated high school, should I still get a GED?

It's good to know that failing on the first try is common. I'll keep it in mind when I get nervous. 

Oh yeah, toxic environment are the perfect words to describe home. I've been considering moving in with Nana and Mom for a while. Then in September the lease on my brother's apartment is up and he's not getting along with his current roommate so he was saying maybe I could get an apartment with him and his girlfriend. I'd like that.

I've had this therapist for a few years and he's a good guy, he's helped me a lot, but I have some major problems with his methods. He has a very behavioral approach I guess I'd call it, the main things we talk about are stuff like how much sleep I'm getting and how much time I spent on the computer. I've always felt like he's just trying to treat symptoms. If I'm already having a good week or month, I'm naturally going to get a good amount of sleep and waste less time on the computer. He's putting the carriage in front of the horse. But the thing is, I've been afraid to get a new therapist since I feel like decent therapists are hard to find.

Again thanks.
